**Why each of the three went `gone`**

- **`mastermind-figma-cards` and `mastermind-test`:** both were refused as "landed" in `revive` log lines in `servex.jsonl`. `Agents.blocked()` buried any agent whose task dir had a landing line. These are long-lived masterminds that landed one task and kept working on others.
- **`mastermind-item`:** I confirmed the same "landed" refusal in the 21:11 sweep. The 21:30 snapshot then listed it already `gone`.
- **Queued (`test` in your note):** its registry row shows it idle with a task dir under `core/Test/tasks/test-system`, and the 21:30 sweep refused `mastermind-test` as "landed". So the landed check is the cause I can show. I couldn't pin down a separate "never started" case for it from the logs.

**What I changed** (all in `Servex/agents/Agents.js` and `Servex/Servex.js`)

- **Landed check:** the boot sweep no longer applies it. A deleted cwd and a stop on purpose still refuse. The spawn-queue restore also skips it for a held resume.
- **Reason on the row:** every agent the sweep buries now gets the reason written on its registry row's `ended` field. Before, the reason was only in the log.
- **Never-started agents:** a revivable row with no completed turn and no session file used to be buried as dead. It now restarts fresh from its own spec and is told where its `requirements.md` is. This is a different failure from the three above, which I found while writing the test. Its original prompt isn't kept on the row, so it relies on that pointer.

**What now happens**
- **Evidence on `complete`:** `Task.complete` takes `{outcome, evidence, confidence, caveats}` (in `core/Task/Task.js`). With no evidence, with a plain string, or with an unknown confidence, it refuses and the message says what to pass.
- **Item tool:** it refuses a `complete` without evidence before it writes a line (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js`). Writing the line first would have let it replay as a finished task.
- **Caveats:** a task that completes with caveats appends one line to its parent's log. It finds the parent the way `SessionRecord.parent_log` does.
- **`approve`** now leaves the task accepted (`idle`); the agent's own `start` begins it.
- **Tab spawns:** `spawn_agent` takes a new `session_id`, the tab's own Claude session id. Servex uses the registered agent for that session as the parent, or registers `vscode-<id8>` if there is none. This is in `Servex/agents/tools.js`, and a tab has to pass `session_id` for it to work.
- **Node-started spawns:** `review.mjs` (both reviewer spawns), `owner-check.mjs` and `clarity.mjs` now pass the triggering task's agent as `parent`. I added `SessionRecord.task_agent(dir)` to look it up.
- **Docs:** `core/Task/readme.md` and the examples in `messaging.md`, `ProcessRunner.js` and `Servex.js` now show evidence. Both items are ticked ✅ in `resolution.md`.

The chase is built and committed as `7db9494a5` in the `task-chase` worktree, not merged. One existing test, `TaskLoop-launch.test.mjs`, fails, and the failure comes from the `approve` change, not this work.

- **Every started task:** the opt-in gate is gone. A started task with no new log line for 5 minutes gets one status ask: title, path, "add a line or complete/stop it". It is asked again every 5 minutes while it stays silent. Accepted, proposed, paused, stopped and complete tasks are never asked.
- **Flag:** after three asks with no new line, or when the agent's last line says it is blocked, one red flag goes to the board using the existing card path. A further flag follows once per hour while it stays silent, and any new line resets the count.
- **State and Heartbeat:** the ask and flag counts are `ask` and `flag` lines on the task's own log, so a restart keeps them. A stopped agent is woken the usual way unless it was stopped on purpose, and if Heartbeat already has a check out for that agent, TaskLoop waits.
- **Docs updated:** `Servex/doc/task-loop.md`, `resolution.md` section 8 (build item ticked ✅) and the "What chases a task today" list in `cracks.md`. `Servex/readme.md` was not checked.

**How "read" is marked:** I reused the mark `Heartbeat.inbox()` already writes. A `{read_upto, at, by}` line is appended to the inbox itself. Unread lines are the ones with `text` after the last such line.

**Row 1, every inbox read:** `read_inboxes()` runs each tick over the task dirs of the last 30 days.
- A live agent gets all its unread lines as one message, then the mark.
- A stopped or gone agent keeps them unread, and the inbox gets one card. An `{inbox_card}` line stops a second card until new lines arrive.
- A line older than 7 days is marked read with a note and never delivered.

**Row 5, waiting on anyone:** `remind_other()` handles a wait on an agent id or a task path. A task path resolves to that task's owning agent. After the follow-up interval (default 120 min), and again each interval, that agent is told "Task x is waiting on you for <what>". After 3 reminders with no change there is one flag card, then nothing more.

**Docs:** rows 1 and 5 of `cracks.md` now say what closes them, and `Servex/doc/task-loop.md` has a new section.

**Decisions**
- The inbox sweep only covers the last 30 days of task dirs, so older unread inboxes stay unread. To reach the full 454-line backlog, raise `inbox_days`.
- The flag after 3 reminders posts a card but does not use the chase's own flag function, because that function's text is about a silent started task.
